issues.description: The UML/problem specification defines the Ride attribute as 'abbreviation: char', but the reference implementation uses a different attribute name ('shortName' of type char) and a corresponding getter getShortName(). This name mismatch between the UML/problem statement and the solution can confuse students about the exact attribute name and expected getter (e.g., getAbbreviation() vs getShortName()).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute name consistent across artifacts. Either rename the Ride attribute in the solution and template from 'shortName' to 'abbreviation' and provide getAbbreviation(), or update the UML/problem statement to use 'shortName' and document getShortName() as the expected getter. Ensure constructor parameter names and order remain consistent with the UML ordering requirement.

issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines Ride with an attribute named 'abbreviation' (char), but the solution implementation names the corresponding field 'shortName' and provides getShortName(). This creates a naming mismatch between the specification and the implemented identifier (and therefore the expected getter name), which can confuse students mapping UML attributes to class fields/getters.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifier names: rename the field 'shortName' to 'abbreviation' in Ride (and update its constructor parameter name and getter to getAbbreviation()), or update the UML/problem statement to use 'shortName' consistently. Ensure constructors and getters across subclasses and usages use the chosen name.
